quickAnswer: Utility gas heats 64.6% of occupied Wayland homes, the 5th-highest share among the 50 towns we serve, while bottled gas heats only 2.1%. The median home dates to 1961, so a new furnace or boiler often comes down to sizing correctly for a mid-century house.
body: ## Gas first, oil second, hardly any propane

According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022), Wayland has 4,949 occupied homes, and 3,196 of them burn utility gas. At 64.6% that is the 5th-highest gas share of the 50 towns we serve, set against 41.9% in the middle town.
Fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,211 homes (24.5%), electricity 418 (8.4%) and bottled gas only 104 (2.1%). That last figure ranks 45th of 50, so the propane tank is a small part of the story here.

For a gas household, a failed boiler is mostly a matching exercise: new equipment, the right size, the right venting. For the roughly one home in four that uses oil, the choice is wider. Stay with oil, convert if the gas company says a main passes the property, or move toward a heat pump. A census table cannot tell you which street has a main, but a phone call to the gas company can.
## Mid-century houses and what they ask of a heating system

The median Wayland home was built in 1961, which is the 3rd-oldest median among the 50 towns (the middle town is 1975). Of 5,130 housing units, 3,488 predate 1980, or 68.0%, the 10th-highest share. The biggest band is 1940 to 1959 with 1,634 units (31.9%), and 1960 to 1979 adds another 1,027 (20.0%).
Units dated 1939 or earlier number 827, or 16.1%, which ranks only 27th. So the weight of the stock sits in the middle decades rather than in the oldest ones.

Houses from the 1940s through the 1970s often carry less insulation than newer construction, and their pipes or ducts may have been laid out for equipment that has since changed. Sizing a replacement from the old nameplate can leave it too big or too small. That is why we assess the home's heating load before we quote a system.
## Owners, detached houses and a high-value market

Single-family detached houses are 4,139 of Wayland's housing units, or 80.7%, which ranks 21st. Owners occupy 4,529 households (91.5%), and renters hold 420 (8.5%), 42nd of 50. Buildings with two or more units account for 546 units, 10.6%, ranking 38th.

The median value of an owner-occupied home is $862,700, the 10th-highest of the 50 towns and far above the $579,150 of the middle town. A house worth that much usually gets a heating or cooling system chosen for the long haul, so our free written estimates come before any work starts and let you compare options at the kitchen table.
## From Sudbury Plantation to Wayland

Wayland was the first settlement of Sudbury Plantation in 1638. After residents split in 1722 the eastern parish became the part we now call Wayland. It was incorporated as East Sudbury on April 10, 1780, and town meeting voted on March 11, 1835, to rename it for Dr. Francis Wayland.

A state law of 1851 enabling free public libraries grew out of a dispute here, and the current library building dates from 1900. The town covers 15.9 square miles and borders Lincoln, Sudbury, Weston, Framingham and Natick, touching Concord only narrowly.
## Rebates depend on the meter

Heat pump rebates run through the utility that serves your address, and that can differ from street to street. Confirm it first, then read the details on the [heat pump page](/cities/wayland/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Is natural gas available on my street in Wayland?
faq.a: Possibly, but the census cannot say. Utility gas serves 3,196 Wayland homes, yet a given street may or may not have a main. Ask the gas company before pricing a conversion from oil, and ask what connecting your property would involve, because that answer decides whether the switch is worth comparing.

faq.q: My Wayland house dates from the 1950s. Does that change the system I should buy?
faq.a: It can. The 1940 to 1959 band holds 1,634 Wayland homes, and insulation, air sealing and ductwork vary a great deal inside it. The right size comes from the house as it stands today, not from the unit you are replacing, which is the reason a heating load assessment comes first.

faq.q: Which heat pump rebate applies to my Wayland home?
faq.a: That depends on the electric utility serving your address, so confirm it first. If the Mass Save path applies, the 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, and the house must be weatherized enough to qualify. Terms can change, so check masssave.com or ask your utility.

faq.q: Should I worry about my boiler after basement flooding in Wayland?
faq.a: Yes, have it inspected before you run it again. Water can damage burners, controls and wiring, and a unit that still starts may be unsafe. If the heating equipment got wet, call (508) 786-8755 and describe what the water reached. A written estimate will lay out repair and replacement options.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Wayland counts 3,196 homes on utility gas, 1,211 on oil or kerosene and 104 on bottled gas. A replacement starts from the fuel already in the basement and, for gas equipment, ends with a permit and an inspection.
body: ## Three fuels, three kinds of replacement
The ACS 2022 puts 3,196 Wayland homes on utility gas and 1,211 on fuel oil or kerosene, with 104 on bottled or tank gas. Each group faces a different job when the old unit gives out.

A gas home usually needs the new appliance matched to the existing gas line, venting and flue. An oil home can renew the oil system, convert if a main is available, or add a heat pump for part of the load. A bottled gas home has a tank arrangement to think about as well. Oil heats a smaller slice of Wayland than of most towns we serve: its 24.5% share ranks 37th of 50, against 36.5% in the middle town.
### The permit step

Only licensed plumbers and gas fitters may pull gas permits in Massachusetts, and swapping in a new gas furnace or boiler normally means a permit plus a final inspection. Ask your contractor who files it, and check with the town's building department if anything is unclear.
### Renters and landlords

Wayland has 420 renter households, 8.5% of the total and 42nd of 50 for renter share. State sanitary code 105 CMR 410.201 asks landlords to hold rental units at 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight during the heating season, usually with the landlord paying for heat. That is general information, not legal advice.
### When the heat quits at night
A boiler that cycles on and off every few minutes, or a furnace that only blows cool air, deserves a prompt call instead of a wait. Emergency calls are taken around the clock at (508) 786-8755.
### What a good repair-or-replace conversation covers

Which part failed, how old the unit is and what the fuel will cost to run next winter. The [maintenance page](/cities/wayland/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) explains how to keep a replacement running well, and the [heat pump page](/cities/wayland/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers the electric route.

faq.q: Is it worth converting an oil boiler to gas in Wayland?
faq.a: It depends on whether a gas main reaches your street and what the connection would require. Utility gas heats 64.6% of Wayland homes, so many neighbors have made that choice, but a heat pump or a new oil boiler can still win for a particular house. Compare the written estimates side by side before deciding.

faq.q: My Wayland rental has no heat tonight. What should I do?
faq.a: Tell the landlord in writing, since unless the lease says otherwise the landlord is responsible for heat. If you manage the building, call us for an emergency visit at (508) 786-8755. Space heaters are a stopgap, not a fix, and a boiler that fails in a cold snap should be looked at promptly.

faq.q: How do I know whether to repair or replace a furnace?
faq.a: Start with the failed part and the age of the unit. One inexpensive part on a younger furnace is usually a repair. A cracked heat exchanger or repeated breakdowns on an old unit point toward replacement. Ask for the options in writing so the decision rests on the whole picture and not on one bad night.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Wayland has 4,139 detached houses plus 546 homes in multi-unit buildings, and a median build year of 1961. Cooling options run from central air where ducts allow to ductless mini-splits where they do not.
body: ## Cooling a town of detached houses

Of Wayland's 5,130 housing units, 4,139 are single-family detached and 438 are attached townhouses. The remaining units sit in buildings of two or more: 206 in two-unit buildings, 119 in buildings of three or four units and 221 in buildings of five or more. Each type cools differently, which makes the building, not the equipment catalog, the place to start.
### Detached houses

A detached house with room for an air handler and a duct run can take central air. One without that room can take ductless heads on the walls. Houses heated by hot-water radiators or baseboard often have no ducts to reuse. Plenty of older houses predate central air, and the 1961 median here puts the typical Wayland house in that company.
### Townhouses and apartments

Attached homes share walls, so the outdoor unit needs a spot that respects the neighbors. In an apartment, one ductless head or a small multi-head system can cool the living area without touching the rest of the building.
### Questions to settle before a quote

- Which rooms overheat, and at what time of day.
- Where an outdoor unit can sit and how far the line set must run.
- Whether the electrical panel has room for new equipment.
- Whether a heat pump that cools in summer and heats in winter would suit the house better than cooling alone.
### Why bigger is not better
A unit that is too large cycles off before the humid air has been dried out. Sizing from this house's insulation, windows and orientation gives steadier summer comfort.
### Repair or replace

A weak capacitor or a dirty coil is often a repair, while a compressor failure on old equipment may point to replacement. About 8.4% of Wayland homes already heat with electricity, and for them a single heat pump can cover both seasons, as the [heat pump page](/cities/wayland/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) explains.

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning to a Wayland house with no ducts?
faq.a: Yes. A ductless mini-split cools without any ductwork, using one outdoor unit and an indoor head for each area. Whether a few heads or a whole-house setup makes sense depends on the layout, how many rooms need cooling and what the heating and cooling load of the house turns out to be.

faq.q: Is one big central unit better than several small ones?
faq.a: Not automatically. Central air suits a house whose ducts are in good shape and reach every room. Several ductless heads suit additions, upper floors and rooms that overheat. A split between the two is common, and the floor plan should settle it.

faq.q: When should I schedule air conditioning service?
faq.a: Spring is the usual time, ahead of the first heat wave. A technician can check refrigerant, coils, drains and electrical parts while the schedule is open. A spring visit tends to catch small problems before a hot week turns them into an urgent call, and it gives you time to plan if the unit is near the end.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Wayland has 1,211 oil or kerosene homes, 104 on bottled gas and 418 on electricity, the three groups with the most to compare against a heat pump. Which rebate applies depends on the utility serving the address.
body: ## Which Wayland homes have the most to weigh

Mass Save's 2026 whole-home program pays $2,650 per ton to a maximum of $8,500, once the house is weatherized. Eligibility details sit on the [heat pump services page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits), and your electric utility decides which program you fall under.
### Oil, bottled gas and electric resistance

A heat pump displaces fuel that is delivered or burned on site, so the 1,211 oil or kerosene homes (24.5%) and the 104 bottled gas homes (2.1%) are the natural place to compare. The 418 homes that heat with electricity (8.4%) can ask whether a heat pump would move the same heat with less power. With 3,196 homes on utility gas, many Wayland owners will instead look at a heat pump for cooling and mild-weather heating.
### Age bands and the weatherization test

The weatherization test uses the year of construction. Wayland counts 860 units from 2000 or later, and 463 of them date from 2010 or later, the 23rd-highest share of the 50 towns. Another 782 units come from 1980 to 1999. For the large mid-century share of the stock, an assessment of the house is the way to see what weatherization work, if any, would be recommended.
### Ducted, ductless or a partial setup

A ducted unit makes sense where ducts are sound. Ductless heads, one per zone, fit a house with radiators or a recent addition. In a hybrid arrangement the existing boiler or furnace stays on standby for the deepest cold, so a working system is not retired early.
### Sizing in a detached house

With 80.7% of units detached, outdoor units usually have exterior wall space. Sizing is the real risk: too small and it cannot keep up in January, too large and it cycles too often. For that reason the load calculation precedes any quote. The [cooling page](/cities/wayland/air-conditioning-installation-repair) shows how the same equipment handles summer.

faq.q: Will my Wayland house pass the heat pump rebate screening?
faq.a: Your utility, a 2026 installation by an eligible installer and the weatherization condition all count. A 2000-or-later house meets that last condition by its date; older ones typically go through a Home Energy Assessment first. Because terms can change, confirm at masssave.com before signing anything.

faq.q: Must the old Wayland boiler go when a heat pump arrives?
faq.a: No. In a partial-home design the boiler or furnace takes the deepest cold and the heat pump carries the milder months. A partial-home rebate exists with its own per-ton amount and bonuses, listed on the services page, and the installer should explain how the two systems will share the load.

faq.q: Do heat pumps heat well in a Massachusetts winter?
faq.a: Cold-climate models are designed for it. Sizing and installation quality matter more than the brand name on the box, which is why the heating load of your house is calculated before a system is quoted. A system sized for summer cooling alone may fall short in January, so ask how the proposal handles the coldest days.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Wayland has 4,529 owner-occupied households and 1,211 homes burning oil or kerosene. Oil equipment gets a yearly cleaning, gas a yearly safety check, and heat pumps a coil and filter visit.
body: ## A yearly rhythm for owners

Owners occupy 4,529 Wayland households, and for most of them one fall visit and one spring visit is a sensible rhythm. The heating visit comes before the first cold snap, the cooling visit before the first heat wave, and a few habits in between keep small problems small.
### Oil, gas and electric differ

The 1,211 oil homes need an annual cleaning: burner serviced, nozzle and filter changed, combustion checked. Skipping it lets soot build up, which can cut efficiency and bring breakdowns in the coldest weeks. The 3,196 gas homes need the burner, venting and controls checked for safety. Electric systems and heat pumps need their coils, filters and drains looked at.
### A vacant or seasonal house

Wayland counts 181 vacant housing units, a 3.5% vacancy rate against 3.6% in the middle town. A house that sits empty still has a heating system that needs checking before winter, because nobody is home to notice a cold radiator or a tripped breaker.
### Reading the signs of age

Short cycling, new noises, rooms that stay cold and a bill that climbs while your habits stay the same are the usual clues that a unit is near the end. A tune-up is a fair moment to ask how much life is left, so you can budget before a failure forces the issue.

- **Fall:** heating tune-up, filter change, clear space around radiators and vents.
- **Spring:** cooling check, leaves cleared from the outdoor unit, drain line tested.
- **Any time:** a smell, soot near an oil burner or a carbon monoxide alarm means call at once.
### Homework between visits

Swap filters on schedule, keep snow and debris away from outdoor units and look at the thermostat batteries before assuming a failure. Have the fuel, the approximate age and the nameplate details ready when you call. If a visit turns up a system past repair, the [heating page](/cities/wayland/heating-installation-repair) covers replacement.

faq.q: How often should an oil boiler be serviced?
faq.a: Once a year, ahead of the heating season. The cleaning removes soot, replaces the nozzle and filter and confirms that combustion is clean. Wayland has 1,211 oil or kerosene homes, so this is a routine chore for a quarter of the town, and a gas boiler also benefits from a yearly check.

faq.q: Is a tune-up worth it for a heat pump?
faq.a: Yes. Coils and filters collect dust, and condensate drains can clog. A yearly visit keeps airflow and the refrigerant side in order. A ductless unit that runs in both seasons gets more hours than a cooling-only unit, so the check matters for it year round.

faq.q: Should I service a Wayland house that stands empty over the winter?
faq.a: Yes, ideally before the cold arrives. Have the system tested, make sure someone checks the house during cold spells and keep the thermostat at a safe setting. A burst pipe in an unattended house costs far more than a service visit, so treat the empty months as a reason for the check, not an excuse to skip it.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Wayland's housing falls into five age bands, from 827 units dated 1939 or earlier to 860 dated 2000 or later. Wayland's old and new houses tend to have opposite air problems: leaks in one, stale air in the other.
body: ## Five eras of house, five kinds of air

The ACS 2022 sorts Wayland's 5,130 housing units into bands: 827 from 1939 or earlier, 1,634 from 1940 to 1959, 1,027 from 1960 to 1979, 782 from 1980 to 1999 and 860 from 2000 on. How air moves through a building often follows its age.
### The older end of the stock

Gaps around windows, sills and chimneys are the usual leak points in an older house. That dilutes some indoor pollutants, but it also pulls in dust, pollen and damp basement air. Ducts that have run for decades can hold dust, and before any renovation a qualified specialist should test older materials.
### The tighter end of the stock

A house built since 2000 is often much tighter. Without working ventilation, shower steam, kitchen fumes and the off-gassing of new furnishings remain indoors. Check that the bathroom fans and range hood vent outdoors and actually run.
### Water in the neighborhood

The town covers 15.9 square miles, 4.21% of it water. In 2010 torrential rains left the Pelham Island area isolated until the water receded, and flood events like that are a reminder of what damp does to a building. Wet materials can grow mold within days, so drying fast and cleaning properly matter as much as treating the air afterward.
### Humidity through the year
Winter heat dries the air, and summer brings the moisture back. A musty basement might want a dehumidifier, though a leak or poor grading must be cured where it starts.
### Options we can discuss

- Filtration upgrades, with filters changed on schedule.
- A dehumidifier or a humidifier tied to the system.
- Better ventilation for houses that hold their air.
- Duct cleaning only where ducts are dirty or damaged, with the cause fixed so they do not fill again.

A test reports moisture, carbon monoxide or particles only for the moment it is taken. Fixing the source is what keeps the result lasting. For heating-side questions, see the [heating page](/cities/wayland/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. Cleaning earns its cost when you can see dirt or mold inside the ducts, or after pest or renovation damage. Looking at the system first shows whether cleaning would help, and if the cause of the dirt is not fixed, the ducts will fill up again regardless of how well they were cleaned.

faq.q: Why does my newer house feel stuffy?
faq.a: Tighter construction holds in moisture, cooking fumes and odors unless something moves air out. A bathroom fan, a range hood that vents outside or a ventilator that brings in fresh air can help. The 860 Wayland units built in 2000 or later are the likeliest to benefit from a ventilation check.

faq.q: What should I do after water gets into a basement?
faq.a: Dry it quickly, remove wet materials that cannot be dried and have any heating equipment that was touched by water inspected before you use it. Mold can start within days. If the water came from a flood, treat damp insulation and drywall as suspect, and ask a specialist about testing if odors linger.
